title: Yochanan Ben Zakkai Leaves in a Coffin
text:
During the Roman siege of Jerusalem around 70 AD, the city was controlled by zealot factions determined to fight to the end. The Babylonian Talmud tells a story about Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, the leading sage of the time, who believed the city could not hold.

According to the Talmud, the zealots had burned the city's stores of food to force the population to fight, and no one was allowed to leave. Yochanan asked his nephew, a zealot leader, for help. The nephew suggested he pretend to be ill and then dead, since only corpses were carried out of the city for burial. His disciples Eliezer and Joshua carried him out in a coffin, past the guards at the gate.

Once outside, Yochanan went to the Roman commander Vespasian and greeted him as king. Vespasian objected that he was not a king, but at that moment, the story says, a messenger arrived from Rome to tell him he had been made emperor. Vespasian, pleased, offered Yochanan a request. He did not ask Vespasian to spare Jerusalem, which he judged impossible. He asked for the town of Yavneh and its sages, protection for the family of the patriarch Gamaliel, and a physician to heal the starving Rabbi Tzadok.

Jerusalem and the Temple were destroyed. At Yavneh, Yochanan's academy became the center from which rabbinic Judaism was rebuilt without the Temple.
lesson: When you cannot save everything, decide what is truly essential and secure that. A modest, achievable request can preserve the future.
people: Yochanan ben Zakkai, Vespasian, Eliezer ben Hyrcanus, Joshua ben Hananiah
source: Babylonian Talmud, Gittin 56a to 56b; also Avot de-Rabbi Natan, version A, chapter 4
caveat: The story is a rabbinic legend: Vespasian was proclaimed emperor in 69 and had left Judea before the city fell.
